{{Quote|Decorating this place must have cost a fortune. Those statues are made with real aurodium. No wonder the Empire wants this place.|A visitor to [[House Organa (estate)|House Organa]]|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
'''Aurodium''' was a [[Ore/Legends|metal]] that, when mined, purified, and formed into [[ingot]]s, was used as currency in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and other lawless territories where [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] were not accepted, much like [[Nova crystal/Legends|nova crystals]]. Aurodium lacked a specific color, but sparkled.

[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious']] [[Darth Sidious' lightsabers/Legends|Lightsabers]] were partially constructed with aurodium.

Aurodium idols were used as gifts to impress and gain the trust of [[Suudaa Nem'ro]], [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] crime lord of [[Jiguuna]], by an [[Imperial Agent]] of the resurrected [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. This was after the agent recovered them from criminal forces.

In [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], ten large ingots of aurodium were worth three billion credits; however, although the ingots were considered large, all of them were, combined, small enough to keep inside a pouch that was easily concealed on a person.

Aurodium was also made into [[Coin/Legends|coins]]. The aurodium standard was once used as a guarantor for the value of galactic currency, though this was abolished sometime after [[4225 BBY]]; thereafter, [[Bank/Legends|banks]] became the key backers of the [[Republic Treasury Reserve]].

At least up to the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the interior of [[Castle Organa]] featured many statues of real aurodium, ranging in size from the typical to the towering.

==Behind the scenes==
Aurodium is obviously intended to be the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe's equivalent to [[Gold/Legends|gold]]. The first two letters of aurodium, "Au," are the chemical symbol for gold and a common prefix for gold-related words. However, gold has been mentioned in other ''Star Wars'' sources. Its name also resembles [[Wikipedia:rhodium|rhodium]], which is a rarer real-life noble metal worth more than gold.
